links.outcome: Ethical alignment of domain-specific fine-tuned mental health models versus their base backbone models
links.effect: Several specialized (fine-tuned) models underperformed their base backbones in ethical alignment across 14 models, so fine-tuning can degrade ethical robustness.
links.quote: Notably, we find that domain-specific fine-tuning can degrade ethical robustness, as several specialized models underperform their base backbones in ethical alignment.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating LLMs against jurisdiction-specific professional ethics guidelines (Australian psychology and psychiatry) using fine-grained ethicality annotations rather than refusal-based safety signals

screen.reason: Empirical benchmarking study introducing PsychEthicsBench to evaluate ethical alignment and safety of 14 large language models in mental health contexts.
